concept.name: Best-interest obligation
concept.definition: The standard of conduct established by the SEC's Regulation Best Interest (Exchange Act Rule 15l-1, adopted 2019) requiring a broker-dealer, when making a recommendation of a securities transaction or investment strategy to a retail customer, to act in the retail customer's best interest without placing its own financial or other interests ahead of the customer's. It is implemented through disclosure, care, conflict-of-interest, and compliance obligations.
concept.intuition: When a broker recommends something to a retail customer, they must recommend what's good for the customer — not what's lucrative for the broker — and prove their house rules back that up.
concept.mechanics: The care obligation requires reasonable diligence, care, and skill to understand the recommendation's risks/rewards/costs, have a reasonable basis for the recommendation to the particular customer, and avoid excessive trading. The disclosure obligation requires revealing material facts about the relationship and conflicts; the conflict obligation requires policies to identify, disclose, and mitigate or eliminate conflicts (with some sales-contest conflicts required to be eliminated).
concept.failure_modes: Reg BI expressly is not a fiduciary duty and permits conflicts to be managed by disclosure and mitigation, so conflicted advice can remain compliant if disclosed; 'best interest' is not judicially defined transaction-by-transaction, making the standard's practical bite dependent on SEC/FINRA examinations.
concept.misconceptions: Reg BI did not make brokers fiduciaries — the SEC deliberately crafted a distinct, enhanced standard above suitability but below the Advisers Act fiduciary duty; and 'best interest' does not mean the cheapest product, since cost is one factor among risks and rewards.
concept.example: A broker recommending one of two similar mutual funds must consider the costs of each; choosing the higher-commission share class without a justification in the customer's interest violates Reg BI's care and conflict obligations.
